input_oneliner: 38M in for AKI from gastroenteritis, sharp central chest pain since evening, changes with breathing and position, HR 96, afebrile

reference_targets_freetext.item: Pericardial friction rub (leaning forward, end-expiration) at the left sternal border
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Rub is the most specific bedside finding for pericarditis

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask whether pain eases sitting forward and worsens supine or with inspiration
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Positional relief is characteristic of pericarditis

reference_targets_freetext.item: Palpate the chest wall and costochondral junctions for fully reproducible tenderness
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Reproducible tenderness supports chest-wall pain after repeated vomiting

reference_targets_freetext.item: Ask about recent viral illness or fever

reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Elevated JVP with effusion supports tamponade

reference_targets_freetext.item: Calf circumference asymmetry >3 cm (10 cm below tibial tuberosity)
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Screens for PE as an alternative cause of pleuritic pain

reference_targets_freetext.item: Compare breath sounds side to side; percuss for unilateral hyperresonance
reference_targets_freetext.rationale: Screens for pneumothorax as an alternative cause of pleuritic pain

should_not_recommend: Use chest-wall tenderness to exclude PE or ACS
Start NSAIDs (contraindicated with active AKI) without examining for effusion/tamponade (JVP, Pulsus paradoxus)
Diagnose by response to a GI cocktail
